newsitem.title: FRANCE: Soc Gen falls on poor sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Soc Gen falls on poor sentiment.

text.p: Shares in French bank Societe Generale fell on Friday as market sentiment turned against its planned acquisition of Credit du Nord from Paribas, traders said.

Part of the sentiment change was attributed to a comment in the Financial Times' Lex column, which cast doubt on the benefits to Societe Generale, given the likely difficulties in cutting costs, particularly through shedding jobs.
Societe Generale traded down 1.09 percent to 546 francs on volume of 121,455 shares at 1248 GMT.
Some analysts shared the newspaper column's view, among them Jerome Labin, analyst at Pinatton who said, "re-establishing profitability for Credit du Nord will not be easy".

On the other hand, the purchase price was fairly low, with Societe Generale paying around two times operating profit while other deals were around three or four times, he said. "Occupying the territory" was a good strategy for Societe Generale, he added.
But another analyst said the deal was an expensive way of acquiring market share.
Paribas shares continued to climb, rising 1.5 percent to 359.5 francs on turnover of 151,540 shares. The transaction is seen as good for Paribas, which is making a capital gain on a mediocre asset.
